key_insight: Boundary geometry can change the optimal shallow ReLU approximation exponent even when dimension, error norm, and coefficient-weighting rule are fixed.
engineering_relevance: For finite ReLU targets, the bounds support compression using only existing neurons without increasing the weighted coefficient sum.
method: Analyze L^q approximation on convex bodies under geometry-aware weighted coefficient constraints.
Prove upper and lower bounds and characterize optimal exponents through small-boundary-cap growth.
Identify sharp weight thresholds that preserve the classical approximation exponent.
evidence_signal: Theoretical guarantees establish optimal exponents for all planar convex bodies and their products with polytopes, plus specified smooth-body regimes; the abstract reports no empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: Optimality guarantees depend on domain geometry and the range of q, so they should not be assumed for every convex body and norm.
paper_title: Boundary Geometry Determines Optimal Shallow ReLU Approximation under Weighted Coefficient Constraints
